audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says 'empowered Q heal' six times and never once states the condition on the heal.
audit.why: Riot's text on Decimate: enemies struck by the BLADE take more damage than those struck by the handle, and Darius heals based on champions hit by the blade. Standing close, inside the handle radius, denies the heal entirely — that is the single most actionable fact in this lane and it was nowhere in either layer.
audit.corrected: phases[3].why, whys[3], spikes[0], early, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0] now state the blade-versus-handle rule and tell you to hug him.

edits.before: Darius wins levels 1 through 3 cleanly — his passive bleed stacks from any touch, and his E pull at 5 stacks into empowered Q heal is a kill threat your W-shield alone cannot reliably eat at low HP totals. Your job is to keep stacks below 3: do not extend autos when his E is off cooldown (24 seconds), farm with Q tip from max range, and pop W reactively the instant his pull animation fires to absorb the bleed burst. If you land a full charged-Q knockup before he closes the gap, that stun buys time for his Hemorrhage to clear and resets the trade firmly in your favor — but the charge telegraph is slow enough that he can simply step back out of the cone. Respect the range on his passive-proc autos; one free Q-heal trade snowballs into an unkillable bleed window.
edits.after: Darius wins levels 1 through 3 cleanly — his passive bleed stacks from any touch, and his E pull at 5 stacks into a blade-edge Decimate is a kill threat Soul Furnace alone cannot eat at low HP totals. Your job is to keep stacks below 3: do not extend autos when Apprehend is up (26 seconds at rank 1), farm with Q tip from max range, and if he does close, stand inside him so Decimate catches you with the handle rather than the healing blade. Pop W the instant his pull animation fires. If you land a full charged-Q knockup before he closes, that stun buys time for Hemorrhage to fall off — but the telegraph is slow enough that he can step back out of the cone. One free blade-edge Decimate snowballs into an unkillable bleed window.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 remain Darius-favored if he built an HP lead, but his all-in damage no longer grows at the same rate and your W-shield starts absorbing a meaningful fraction of a 5-stack trade. At level 6 you gain Unstoppable Onslaught — the charge lets you gap-close from outside his E range, and if you R into him when his E is on cooldown you dictate the fight rather than reacting to his pull. His R execute still ends the fight if he stacks to 5 before you threaten the knockup, so the key habit is charging Q BEFORE his bleed reaches 3 stacks, not after — use E armor-shred to set up the stun rather than trading autos building his passive. This is when the lane becomes genuinely even: neither of you can freely win the all-in without hitting your setup first.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 remain Darius-favored, but his all-in damage no longer grows at the same rate and Soul Furnace absorbs a meaningful fraction of a 5-stack trade. At level 6 you gain Unstoppable Onslaught — the charge closes from outside Apprehend's 535 range, and if you commit while the pull is down you dictate the fight instead of reacting to it. Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so no amount of armour saves you at 5 stacks: charge Q BEFORE his bleed reaches 3, not after, and use Roar of the Slayer to set up the stun rather than trading autos into Crippling Strike, whose wind-up is your cue to step back. Neither of you wins the all-in without landing your setup first.
